method: Code read of the named engine/UI files, plus throwaway vitest probes kept in the scratchpad (scratchpad/probe/*.probe.ts, run with a scratchpad config; no repository file touched). 'Probe:' marks a finding confirmed by running it.

findings.problem: A mid-term dismissal (a grave breach while on warning) ends the school's scheduled items but leaves all coursework live. The open assignments stay open, and prepare, choose, approach, ask_partner, answer_partner, respond and make_amends all still work. A partner rehearsal booked after dismissal runs and is 'kept', which moves trust, the bond and listening.
findings.evidence: school.ts:1132-1137 (cancels only pending 'school.*' items); school.ts:2268-2273 (lapseTerm only runs in the EVALUATION handler, which the dismissal cancels); coursework.ts:428-446, 888-909, 1095-1105, 1151-1159 (no standing check); CourseworkPane.tsx:39-46 and looks/school.tsx:176 (open work still shown). Probe: 7 assignments still open after dismissal, ask_partner accepted, rehearsal status 'kept'.
findings.why: A dismissed student keeps doing class work, growing abilities and building bonds with a class they've left, so dismissal does not end school.
findings.suggested_fix: On dismissal or graduation, lapse every open or revising assignment, close open asks and moments, and cancel pending study sessions. Add a shared 'enrolled' guard to the coursework, classmates and production refusals.
findings.tests: school.test.ts and smoke.test.ts cover dismissal cancelling the calendar. Nothing covers coursework after dismissal.

findings.problem: Commencement is booked after the sixth evaluation for any standing short of dismissal, including Academic Warning or Concern, and nothing else is checked: coursework, productions performed, or the You Are The Creator showing. The final-term warning notice still says 'Improve by the end of next term, or you may be dismissed' when there is no next term. The Standing tab gives 'any standing short of dismissal' as the rule, under 'The stages are the Yale Bulletin's'.
findings.evidence: school.ts:1935-1938, 2276-2281, 1147-1148; SchoolWorkspace.tsx:151, 154; tutorial.ts:176 ('After six terms in standing'). Probe: evaluate(term 5) from concern with 0% attendance gave 'warning', Commencement was booked, and the notice said 'by the end of next term'.
findings.why: Graduation can't be failed in the last term, the final warning is an empty threat, and SLATE's rule is presented as Yale's.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide a final-term rule (for example, warning at the last evaluation means no degree, or a remediation period) and check stated degree requirements. Reword the last-term notices. Label the rule as SLATE's estimate.
findings.tests: school.test.ts covers graduating in good standing. Nothing covers graduating on warning.

findings.problem: A booked partner rehearsal that falls while the player is in hospital or laid up counts as standing the partner up: missedByYou, trust -12, bond -5, an incident toward a boundary, and 'X Waited For You'. A hospital admission doesn't cancel or excuse booked rehearsals. This contradicts health.ts's statement that an admission 'is an excused absence everywhere'.
findings.evidence: coursework.ts:916-926; health.ts:336-345. Probe: hospital stay over a booked rehearsal gave status missedByYou and trust 50 -> 38.
findings.why: Getting ill damages relationships and can trigger the 'ask a day ahead' boundary, which punishes something the player can't control.
findings.suggested_fix: When in hospital, laid up or on a called-in sick day, mark the rehearsal 'excused' or cancel it with no trust, bond or incident cost, and tell the player. Do the same for STUDY_KIND.
findings.tests: partners.test.ts doesn't cover hospital. A grep for missedByYou in tests finds nothing.

findings.problem: An excused absence (sick day or hospital) on a course's last meeting of term, or with no later meeting, is treated exactly like an unexcused one: status 'missed', the partner's trust and bond penalised, an incident logged, and the notice 'it isn't taken later'.
findings.evidence: coursework.ts:746-752 (the 'excused && next' branch only; it falls through to missed).
findings.why: A sick student is punished for illness, and the partner blames them.
findings.suggested_fix: If excused and there's no next meeting, set status 'lapsed' (or a new 'excused') with no partner penalty and an accurate notice.

findings.problem: Skipping the revision meeting (unexcused) sets the work to 'done' silently, with no notice, no 'missed' and no effect. The term evaluation then keeps the first showing's band, so missing the reshowing is never worse than giving a weak one.
findings.evidence: coursework.ts:790-795; school.ts:1914 (revision band replaces the first only if it exists).
findings.why: The repeated showing is optional in practice.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the revision as missed, notify, and have the evaluation and notes ledger read it.
findings.tests: school-fixes.test.ts and journey-school-year.test.ts cover revisions shown. Neither covers one missed.

findings.problem: The coursework criterion counts only pieces that were shown. An unexcused 'missed' showing counts as neither shown nor unready, so not turning up is safer than showing unready work.
findings.why: This rewards absence over effort. The cost of one missed class day against the attendance floor is negligible.
findings.suggested_fix: Count unexcused 'missed' pieces as unready in the coursework tally, and in its minimum of three.
findings.tests: None found for missed pieces in evaluate().

findings.stage: Feedback and revisions (double or unearned reward)
findings.problem: noteTaken() treats a dimension note as applied whenever that part is now at 0.8 or above. A note can be given on a part that's already above 0.8: the shortfall is weight x (1 - v) >= 0.05, so up to about 0.93 for a 0.7-weight part. That revision is 'applied' with no work, gets the 1.1 growth weight, resolves the note, and says 'what held it back last time was worked on, and it showed'. The partner part also rises between showings with no player action (partnerOwn grows week by week). The 0.8 threshold doesn't match LEARNING.enough of 0.75.
findings.why: The feedback text claims work that wasn't done, and the revision bonus can be had for free.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure 'taken' as a rise from the note's own level (or require a revise step since the showing), and settle on one threshold.
findings.tests: school-fixes.test.ts and traits-connected.test.ts touch revision. Nothing tests a note given above dimEnough.

findings.problem: A showing's band comes from the evaluation (judgeWork), but its note and strengths come from preparation shortfalls plus a legacy craft score (craftScore < 0.45). The evaluation's own ranked limits are ignored. Work held back by condition (flu, fatigue, the hour) or by an ability can be banded Unready and still be told 'It held together this time. The next step: ...'. 'You came rested and ready' reads focusOf, which skips illness and the hour, not the condition the band used.
findings.why: The note can contradict the band, and players are steered to fix the wrong thing.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick the note from judged.limits[0] (preparation, condition or ability), never give the 'advanced' note on an unready band, and base 'rested' on conditionAt.
findings.tests: feedback.test.ts and learning.test.ts cover the note ledger. None checks that the note agrees with the band.

findings.problem: The button that only marks feedback as read (school.read_feedback) is labelled 'Take The Note'. Elsewhere, 'Taken' means a note applied: KIND_LABEL applied, the ledger's 'Taken <date>', and 'The Note Was Taken'.
findings.why: Players believe the note is dealt with when they've only opened it.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel it 'Read The Note' or 'Mark Read'.

findings.problem: Only practice checks commitmentWithin. Plays.read (120 minutes), school.prepare (up to 105), school.choose, learn_part, review_blocking and work_note (60), orientation catch-up, the 'help' reply (45) and make_amends can all start just before 9 a.m. classes or a 3 p.m. call. advanceTo then runs the class with the player 'present', so both are credited.
findings.evidence: playreading.ts:96-103, 130; coursework.ts:428-446, 475, 1080-1082, 1045; production.ts:257-273, 280; classmates.ts:318-322, 391, 340, 426; life.ts:542-545 (the check that exists); practice.ts:45. Probe: a 2-hour read started at 8:00 ended at 10:00, and the 9:00 classes were attended (attended 1 -> 2).
findings.why: Two hours are lived at once, and the protection practice got on 2026-10-10 is missing everywhere else.
findings.suggested_fix: Add commitmentWithin(minutes), plus the inHospital and asleep checks, to every refusal that advances the clock.

findings.stage: Actions while in hospital or injured
findings.problem: Coursework preparation (including studio and on-your-feet steps with a sprain), table-work choices, production own-work, orientation sessions (the handler and catch-up), the 'help' reply and a run-lines study session all work from a hospital bed. The study session is even 'kept' (it only checks town and awake), while a partner rehearsal at the same time is penalised (finding 3). Practice refuses all of these.
findings.why: Hospital rules are inconsistent between systems, and work done in hospital counts in full.
findings.suggested_fix: Share one 'canWorkNow' refusal (hospital, asleep, injury limits for feet or studio) across these systems.

findings.stage: Line learning (preparation applied to the wrong work)
findings.problem: Running lines with classmate X raises memorization on whichever open scene has the least secure lines, which may be a scene with a different partner or for another course.
findings.why: The work done goes to an unrelated assignment.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply it to the assignment shared with that classmate, or let the player choose.

findings.stage: Blocking and line learning (excused missed call)
findings.problem: An excused missed School or Rep rehearsal (sick day or hospital) returns before callMissed. blockingMissed isn't recorded, so review_blocking refuses with 'You haven't missed any blocking'. An excused absence can't be caught up from the book, but an unexcused one can. The Cabaret and Summer handlers record a gap for any absence.
findings.why: A sick actor goes into the nights under-prepared with no way to recover.
findings.suggested_fix: Call callMissed for excused blocking, tech and dress calls too (the tally stays excused).

findings.problem: cabaretWeek reads an understudy's on-call item as a zero-minute moment at curtain minus three hours, so on-call performance nights never block a Cabaret week. Its own comment ('a night on call doesn't [leave the evening free]'), the guide and the Cabaret panel all claim the week is clear of casting. If the understudy is sent on, both performances happen.
findings.evidence: school.ts:1005-1016 (comment at 1014), 1833; SchoolWorkspace.tsx:489; tutorial.ts:175. Probe: a first-year Seagull understudy joined the week of 18 Mar 2027, and 6 Cabaret calls (all three evening shows among them) coincide with Seagull performances they're on call for.
findings.why: The player can be double-booked, and the stated guarantee is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat on-call items as occupying perfAt to perfAt + 180 minutes in cabaretWeek, and in take_shift, ask_partner and study clash checks.
findings.tests: school.test.ts covers the Cabaret against casting calls, not on-call nights.

findings.problem: take_shift only avoids items with requiresPlayer, so a 7-11 p.m. elective shift can land on an understudy's performance night. If sent on, both the shift and the performance are credited. Elective 'front of house at Yale Rep' shifts are also offered in the summer recess, before the first term and in weeks when the Rep is dark: shiftRefusal checks only standing and hours.
findings.why: The player can be double-booked, and paid work appears in a dark theater.
findings.suggested_fix: Count on-call nights as conflicts, and limit elective shifts to class periods or Rep run dates.

findings.problem: 'Nobody on academic warning may take part' is checked only when joining. A breach that puts the student on warning mid-rehearsal leaves the show running. The panel also says 'The chair approves it', but there's no approval step.
findings.why: A stated rule isn't enforced, and an approval is declared that nothing performs.
findings.suggested_fix: Cancel the pending Cabaret calls on warning with a notice, and either model the approval or drop the claim.

findings.problem: The third-year You Are The Creator showing (first Friday of classes, 3-6 p.m.) is booked on top of Shakespeare Repertory Project I's 3-9 p.m. rehearsal for the students cast in it. cast() resolves overlaps only between School and Rep calls, never with labs, so both handlers run and both count.
findings.evidence: school.ts:1252, 1256-1260, 1791, 1827-1829. Probe: labDays(5) = 2029-01-19; rehearsalDays for Shakespeare I includes 2029-01-19 (rank 1). Ranks 8 and 14 are clear.
findings.why: The player is in two places at once on the solo showing, and is credited for both.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave lab days out of rehearsalDays, or put labs into cast()'s overlap resolution.

findings.problem: call_in_sick is refused unless today has classes. Flu on a Saturday (Saturday Rep performances, the assigned shift, which ignores sickDay), in the spring recess (the Seagull run spans it), in the May work period (Carlotta performances), or in the week before classes (rehearsalDays starts at term start) can't be excused.
findings.why: Being ill on the wrong day carries more risk than on a class day.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow calling in sick for any day with a school commitment, and have shifts read sickDay.
findings.tests: school.test.ts and condition-reach.test.ts cover class days only.

findings.problem: The guide says two missed calls in a term, 'labs and rehearsals together', take you out of the casting pool. The lab handler counts the miss but never checks missedCallsOut and sends no notice. The check only fires at the next missed rehearsal or run-through.
findings.why: Missed labs are silent, and the stated rule is only half true.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the same castable check and notice in the lab handler.

findings.problem: After a December dismissal, Yale Health cover runs to 1 August of the next year, but the spring term's plan premium is never billed, because the TERM handler returns early for a dismissed student.
findings.why: Dismissal grants about seven months of free insurance, so ending school doesn't end its benefits consistently.
findings.suggested_fix: End cover at the end of the last paid term, or bill the plan through the cover's end.
findings.tests: A grep for yaleUntil in tests finds nothing. permission.test.ts covers status after dismissal.

findings.problem: The guide still says 'At the degree, your monologues are filmed.' The filmed-monologues mark was removed on 2026-10-10 and nothing films anything. content/school.ts LABS doc still lists 'the filmed monologues posted at the end of the final term'.
findings.why: It promises a declared word that nothing reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove it or put it in the past tense.

findings.problem: The DRAM 793b template still sells 'the industry showcase' and 'in front of agents there's no second take'. Its doc comment says the scene 'reads at the showcase (showcaseSceneSeen in systems/career.ts)', but that file was deleted on 2026-10-09.
findings.why: It describes an outcome that no longer exists, a present-tense claim the code contradicts.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the comment in the past tense, and reword the deliverable and notes as a class showing.

findings.problem: The Casting tab's fine print says the chair reads 'how the last run's nights went'. Since 2026-10-10 the chair reads delivery, not the nights' bands, and the Why This Cast panel on the same tab says the nights 'isn't read here'.
findings.why: The tab contradicts itself about what casting rewards.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword it to fit, plus a fifth by delivery, plus the balance of opportunity.

findings.problem: The playreading header says that after school 'the library of the town whose card you hold' lends plays. The code refuses every read after school.
findings.why: Stale claim. Post-school play reading is impossible, so the 'Plays To Read' panel is dead after the degree.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the header in the past tense, or give post-school reading a source.

findings.problem: 'From Your Teachers' shows invented term notes under real, named Yale faculty ('Gregory Wallace, Acting I: ...') with no 'simulated' marker. Coursework feedback and the looking-back text both carry one.
findings.evidence: SchoolWorkspace.tsx:160-171; school.ts:1461-1477; compare CourseworkPane.tsx:237 and production.ts:363.
findings.why: Made-up words are attributed to real people.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Simulated: the game's words, not theirs', as the coursework does.

findings.problem: The guide and the Seagull panel say 'the Rep calls at five on each performance day'. The check runs three hours before curtain, which is 11 a.m. for Sunday 2 p.m. matinees. The on-call explanation is only shown for The Seagull (term 1), not for later understudies.
findings.why: A player away on a Sunday morning breaches while thinking they have until five.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'three hours before curtain' and show the panel for every understudy casting.

findings.problem: The 'Registration And Your Account' and 'Meeting The Acting Faculty' sessions only return text. Missing registration changes nothing, yet the panel says 'each session changes what you know or have arranged'. 'classmates' only sets met, which the first class sets anyway.
findings.why: Under THE ONE RULE these are declared steps that nothing reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire registration to something real (for example the scholarship or shift booking), or reword the panel.

findings.stage: UI offering what the engine refuses
findings.problem: Table-work selects are enabled whatever the familiarity or occupancy, but school.choose refuses with 'Read it first', and the select snaps back. Call In Sick is shown whenever today's classes are pending, even when the player is well, and the command refuses. The Cabaret and Summer join buttons disappear with no reason shown.
findings.evidence: CourseworkPane.tsx:147 vs coursework.ts:1078-1081; SchoolWorkspace.tsx:256-266 vs school.ts:2511; SchoolWorkspace.tsx:477, 508.
findings.why: Dead clicks and unexplained missing actions.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable controls with the engine's refusal as the title text, as the prepare buttons already do.

findings.problem: An hour of work_note on a director's 'find more <skill>' note marks it taken at the next call, and that call gets the 1.1 weight, however the skill moved. A coursework 'skill' note ('that's the work for the next weeks') counts as taken once revision prep reaches 0.6.
findings.why: Working on a note and applying it are treated as the same thing.
findings.suggested_fix: For skill notes, require a measurable rise in that skill, or call it 'worked on' rather than 'taken'.

findings.problem: A first-year's Carlotta rehearsals after the April evaluation go into a tally that the next fall resets, so their attendance is never weighed. Only the castable flag and breaches reach them.
findings.why: Missing late-term rehearsals costs almost nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry calls that fall after the evaluation into the next term's tally, as runs already are via 'unreviewed'.
findings.tests: coverage-gaps-runs.test.ts covers runs, not call attendance.

findings.problem: The guide says the evaluation weighs only attendance and growth. evaluate() also reads stage work, coursework bands and breaches.
findings.evidence: tutorial.ts:176 vs school.ts:1920; SchoolWorkspace.tsx:151 states all of them.
findings.why: The guide and the screen disagree.
